mainTopic: Can speech cancel earlier speech (רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש), and קידושין 'from now and after thirty days' (רב and שמואל)
overview: The amud opens by finishing a challenge from the laws of כלים, where a thought cannot cancel an earlier thought. The גמרא answers that thought in טומאה counts like an action, as shown by רב פפא's reading of כי יתן / כי יותן. Then רב זביד places the whole argument on a different case: a woman who made a שליח to accept קידושין for her and then took the appointment back with words alone. רבי יוחנן says words can cancel words, and ריש לקיש says they cannot. Each side challenges the other, and ריש לקיש is finally refuted by the case of a husband who cancels the גט he sent. The הלכה follows רבי יוחנן, and the גמרא shows this fits with רב נחמן's ruling, because the husband cancels the שליח but not the גט. The amud then turns to רב and שמואל on a woman betrothed 'from now and after thirty days', which comes down to whether those words are a condition or a change of mind. The amud ends as אביי begins a case of two men with overlapping time periods, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Thought does not even cancel thought in the laws of vessels
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting the rule from the laws of כלים and asks: granted that thought cannot cancel an action, but it should at least cancel an earlier thought.
steps.simpleTranslation: An action cancels an earlier action and an earlier thought. A thought cancels neither an earlier action nor an earlier thought. It makes sense that a thought cannot cancel an action, because speech cannot come and cancel an action. But it should at least cancel an earlier thought!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a rule about when a כלי counts as finished for טומאה. It uses that rule to attack the idea that speech can cancel earlier speech.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule says a later מחשבה cannot cancel an earlier מחשבה. Speech and thought are both 'non-actions', so they seem equal. If one thought cannot cancel another, then one statement should not cancel another either. That goes against the view that a person can cancel his own earlier words.

keyTerms.meaning: A thought or decision, without any physical act
Takes out of the power of, meaning it cancels
But, used here to bring the challenge

steps.confusionAlert: The first two lines are a quoted rule, not the challenge itself. The challenge only starts at בשלמא.

phrases.english: An action takes it out of the power of an earlier action
phrases.notes: This is about a כלי: a later action of working on it cancels its earlier 'finished' status.

phrases.english: and out of the power of an earlier thought.
A thought does not take it out
neither from the power of an action
nor from the power of a thought.
Granted, it does not take it out from an action,
because speech does not come and cancel an action,
but from a thought, at least, it should take it out!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the source quoted at the end of the previous section and turns it into a challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that speech can cancel earlier speech
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the laws of כלים, a thought cannot cancel an earlier thought. So speech, which is also a non-action, should not cancel earlier speech.

steps.title: Thought in impurity counts like an action
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that מחשבה in the laws of טומאה is different, because it is treated like a real action. This follows רב פפא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Thought in the laws of impurity is different, because it is like an action. This is like the view of רב פפא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. In טומאה, a thought is as strong as an action, so only a real action can cancel it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule from כלים does not prove that thought can never cancel thought. In טומאה, the first thought has the strength of a מעשה. Another thought is too weak to cancel it. Regular speech in other areas, like a woman's agreement to קידושין, has no such strength, so later speech can cancel it. The גמרא now points to רב פפא as its source.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is like the view of רב פפא

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a key idea: in טומאה, what a person wants or decides can carry the weight of a physical act.

phrases.english: Thought in the laws of impurity is different,
because it is like an action,
and this is like the view of רב פפא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: thought in טומאה has the power of action, unlike speech elsewhere
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought thought and speech are equally weak everywhere, so the rule of כלים would apply to speech too.
steps.terutzMaskana: Thought in טומאה is like an action, so its rule teaches nothing about speech cancelling speech.

steps.title: רב פפא's question: written כי יתן but read כי יותן
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא points to a clash between how a פסוק is written (כי יתן, 'if he puts') and how it is read (כי יותן, 'if it is put').
steps.simpleTranslation: For רב פפא pointed out a contradiction: it is written 'כי יתן', but we read it 'כי יותן'. How can that be?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רב פפא's teaching. He first sets up a problem in the פסוק about water that makes food able to become טמא. His answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The written spelling means a person actively puts water on the food. The way we read it means the water came onto the food in any way. רב פפא asks how both can be true. This is setup for his answer.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written (the spelling in the text)
We read it (the way it is said aloud)

phrases.english: For רב פפא pointed out a contradiction:
It is written: 'if he puts',
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:38, about water that makes food able to become טמא.

phrases.english: but we read it: 'if it is put'.
How can this be?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the רב פפא source that step 2 relied on.
steps.kashyaTarget: The פסוק כי יתן / כי יותן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The spelling requires an active act, but the reading includes any wetting, so the two seem to clash.

steps.title: Being pleased counts like doing it yourself
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers: 'it is put' must be like 'he puts'. Just as putting water yourself shows you want it, the water that falls on its own only counts when the owner is pleased with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If it is put' is like 'if he puts'. Just as 'he puts' is a case where he is pleased, so too 'it is put' counts only where he is pleased.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא settles the clash. Water that came onto the food by itself counts only if the owner is pleased with it. This shows that in טומאה, wanting something works like doing it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reading widens the case to water that falls without any action. The spelling limits it to cases like an action, where the owner wants it. So the owner's attitude, a מחשבה, stands in for a מעשה. This proves step 2: thought in טומאה is like action, so only an action can cancel it.

keyTerms.meaning: He is pleased with it, it suits him

steps.whatToRemember: In טומאה, wanting something (ניחא ליה) counts like doing it. That is why the rule of כלים, where thought cannot cancel thought, teaches nothing about speech cancelling speech.

phrases.english: 'If it is put' is like 'if he puts'.
Just as 'he puts' is where he is pleased with it,
so too 'it is put' is where he is pleased with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's question from step 3, and so supports the answer in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Combining the written form and the read form of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Either only active putting counts, or any wetting at all counts.
steps.terutzMaskana: Wetting counts when the owner is pleased with it. Being pleased works like an action.

steps.title: רב זביד's version: the woman who sent an agent
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד taught this argument on a different case: a woman who allowed her שליח to accept קידושין for her, then accepted קידושין herself. Whichever קידושין came first is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד taught this discussion on the following case: And similarly, a woman who gave permission to her agent to accept קידושין for her, and then she went and accepted קידושין herself. If hers came first, her קידושין is valid. If her agent's came first, her קידושין is not valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives a second version of the whole discussion. רב זביד taught it on the case of a woman, her שליח, and קידושין. This step quotes that case, and the argument itself comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case comes from the משנה: whichever קידושין happened first takes effect. Here she acted herself, which is a real action. רב זביד attaches the debate about whether speech cancels speech to this case, and the next step asks what happens if she only takes back the appointment with words.

keyTerms.meaning: He taught this discussion on this case
Betrothal, the first stage of marriage

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument. It is the same debate, taught by רב זביד on a different case.

phrases.aramaic: רַב זְבִיד מַתְנֵי לְהָא שְׁמַעְתְּתָא אַהָא:
phrases.english: רב זביד taught this discussion on this case:
And similarly, a woman who gave permission
to her agent to accept קידושין for her,
and she went and accepted קידושין herself,
phrases.notes: She accepted it from someone else, not from the man her agent was dealing with.

phrases.english: if hers came first, her קידושין is valid,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם שֶׁל שְׁלוּחָהּ קָדְמוּ – אֵין קִידּוּשֶׁיהָ קִידּוּשִׁין.
phrases.english: and if her agent's came first, her קידושין is not valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב זְבִיד מַתְנֵי לְהָא שְׁמַעְתְּתָא אַהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the whole discussion, placed on a different case from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a woman and her שליח both arrange קידושין, whichever came first is valid. רב זביד places the debate on this case.

steps.title: What if she just takes back the appointment?
steps.stepSummary: In רב זביד's version, the גמרא asks about a woman who did not accept קידושין herself but only said she cancels her שליח.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she did not accept קידושין herself, but only took back the appointment, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a new question inside רב זביד's version. There is no action here, only words taking back earlier words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5 she accepted קידושין herself, and that was a real act. Here she only speaks. So the question is whether speaking alone can undo the earlier appointment of the שליח.

keyTerms.meaning: She took it back, she changed her mind

phrases.english: She did not betroth herself
but she retracted, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא קִדְּשָׁהּ אֶת עַצְמָהּ וְחָזְרָה בָּהּ, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the case where she acted herself (step 5) to a case where she only spoke.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can spoken words alone cancel an earlier appointment of a שליח for קידושין?

steps.title: Can words cancel earlier words?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says she can take it back, because words can cancel words. ריש לקיש says she cannot, because words cannot cancel words.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says she can take it back, and ריש לקיש says she cannot. רבי יוחנן says she can, because a statement can cancel a statement. ריש לקיש says she cannot, because a statement cannot cancel a statement.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question in opposite ways, and the גמרא spells out the reason behind each answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making someone a שליח is done with words. רבי יוחנן holds that new words are strong enough to undo old words. ריש לקיש holds that only an action can undo the appointment, so words alone do nothing.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן says a דיבור cancels a דיבור. ריש לקיש says it does not.
steps.confusionAlert: This is רב זביד's version of the argument, about a woman taking back her appointment of a שליח. Don't mix it up with the first version earlier on the daf. That version was about a woman who accepted money for קידושין meant to take effect after thirty days, and then changed her mind.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says: She can retract,
and Reish Lakish says: She cannot retract.
Rabbi Yoḥanan says she can retract,
because a statement comes and cancels a statement.
Reish Lakish says she cannot retract,
because a statement does not come and cancel a statement.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: חוֹזֶרֶת, וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: אֵינָהּ חוֹזֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6 with a dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: a דיבור cancels an earlier דיבור, so she can retract. ריש לקיש: it does not, so she cannot.

steps.title: Challenge from the cancelled תרומה agent
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש from a משנה: if the owner cancelled before the agent separated תרומה, the agent's תרומה does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן challenged ריש לקיש: If he cancelled, and he cancelled before the agent separated, the agent's תרומה is not תרומה!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן quotes a משנה that seems to show an owner can cancel his agent, which looks like words cancelling words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner appointed the agent with words. If 'cancelled' means he just said he takes it back, then the משנה proves words cancel words, against ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to a כהן

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan raised an objection to Reish Lakish:

phrases.aramaic: בִּיטֵּל, אִם עַד שֶׁלֹּא תָּרַם בִּיטֵּל –
phrases.english: If he cancelled, if he cancelled before the agent separated,
phrases.notes: This is from משנה תרומות 3:4, about an owner who sent an agent to separate תרומה for him.

phrases.english: his teruma is not teruma!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks ריש לקיש's position from step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's rule that a דיבור cannot cancel a דיבור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says cancelling the agent works, which looks like words undoing the words of appointment.

steps.title: רבא: the owner cancelled by acting
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the משנה is talking about an owner who separated תרומה himself first, which is a real action.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What case are we dealing with here? Where the owner went first and separated תרומה from his pile himself, which counts as an action.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends ריש לקיש by reading 'cancelled' in the משנה as an action, not just words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the owner already took תרומה from the pile, there is nothing left for the agent to do. That is an action, and everyone agrees an action can cancel words. So the משנה proves nothing about words cancelling words.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here?

phrases.english: Rava says:
With what are we dealing here?
With a case where the owner went first
and separated teruma from his pile,
which counts as an action.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Cancelled' means the owner just said he takes back the agency.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Cancelled' means he separated תרומה himself, an action, so ריש לקיש's rule still stands.

steps.title: Challenge from thought in the laws of כלים
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש challenges רבי יוחנן from a משנה in כלים: thought cannot cancel an earlier thought.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש challenged him: All vessels become able to get טמא through thought, but leave that state only through a change made by an action. An action cancels both an earlier action and an earlier thought. A thought cancels neither an earlier action nor an earlier thought. Fine that thought cannot cancel an action, since a statement cannot cancel an action. But it should at least cancel a thought!
steps.whatsHappening: Now ריש לקיש fights back. He quotes a משנה that says thought does not cancel thought, which seems to go against רבי יוחנן's rule that words cancel words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Thought is like words: neither is an action. The משנה says a later thought cannot undo an earlier thought. That seems to prove that one non-action cannot cancel another, against רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: A change made by an action

phrases.english: Reish Lakish raised an objection to him:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַכֵּלִים יוֹרְדִים לִידֵי טוּמְאָתָן בְּמַחְשָׁבָה,
phrases.english: All vessels go down into their state of impurity through thought,
phrases.notes: He means they become finished vessels that can get טמא once the owner decides to do no more work on them.

phrases.english: and they do not come up from their impurity
except through a change made by an action.

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲשֶׂה מוֹצִיא מִיַּד מַעֲשֶׂה וּמִיַּד מַחְשָׁבָה,
phrases.english: An action takes it out of the status set by an action and by a thought;
a thought does not take it out

phrases.aramaic: לֹא מִיַּד מַעֲשֶׂה וְלֹא מִיַּד מַחְשָׁבָה.
phrases.english: neither from an action nor from a thought.
Granted, it does not take it out from an action,
because a statement does not come and cancel an action,
but it should at least take it out from a thought!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 9 defended ריש לקיש, ריש לקיש now attacks רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that a דיבור cancels a דיבור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says thought cannot cancel thought. If non-actions cannot cancel each other, words should not cancel words.

steps.title: Thought in טומאה counts like an action
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that thought in the laws of טומאה is special, because it is treated like an action. This follows רב פפא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Thought in the laws of טומאה is different, because it is like an action, and this follows רב פפא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן defends his rule by saying the משנה in כלים is a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the earlier thought counts like an action, then a later thought cannot undo it, just as words cannot undo an action. So the משנה does not prove that words cannot cancel words in general.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Thought in the laws of impurity is different,
because it is like an action,
and this follows Rav Pappa.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי מַחְשָׁבָה דְּטוּמְאָה דְּכִי מַעֲשֶׂה דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Making a distinction (special status of thought in טומאה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Thought in כלים is a regular non-action, just like words.
steps.terutzMaskana: Thought in טומאה counts like an action, so it cannot be undone by a later thought. Words in general can still cancel words.

steps.title: רב פפא: written one way, read another
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא points out that a פסוק is written 'if he puts' but read 'if it is put'.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רב פפא raised a contradiction: It is written 'if he puts,' but we read 'if it is put.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רב פפא's source. He first sets up a problem: the written and read forms of a word do not match.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'He puts' sounds like the person must put the water on himself. 'It is put' sounds like any water counts, even water that fell by itself. We need to know which one the תורה means.

phrases.english: As Rav Pappa raises a contradiction:
It is written: "if he puts,"
and we read: "if it is put."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source behind step 11's claim.
steps.kashyaTarget: The meaning of the פסוק about water on produce.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The written form and the read form point in different directions.

steps.title: Water only counts when the owner wants it
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that 'it is put' must be like 'he puts': water counts only when the owner is happy with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? 'It is put' is like 'he puts.' Just as 'he puts' means he is happy with it, so too 'it is put' means he is happy with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא solves the problem by joining both readings: even water that falls on its own counts, but only if the owner wants it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So in טומאה, what the owner wants decides the law, just like an action would. That is why רבי יוחנן says thought in טומאה is like an action, and the challenge from כלים is answered.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? How do the two fit?

steps.whatToRemember: In טומאה, what a person wants works like an action. That is why רבי יוחנן can say words cancel words, and still agree that thought does not cancel thought in כלים.

phrases.english: How so?
"If it is put" is like "if he puts";
just as "he puts" means he is pleased with it,
so too "it is put" means he is pleased with it.
phrases.notes: He means water that fell by itself also makes the produce able to get טמא, if the owner is happy it got wet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Solves the contradiction of step 12 and so supports step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Joining the written and read forms
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Either only water put on by the person counts, or any water counts.
steps.terutzMaskana: Any water counts, but only if the owner wants it. So what the owner wants acts like a real action in טומאה.

steps.title: A husband can cancel a גט he sent just by speaking
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש from a case where a husband cancels his שליח's mission with words alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן challenged ריש לקיש: If a man sends a גט to his wife, and then he catches up with the שליח, or sends a second שליח after him, and says, 'The גט I gave you is canceled,' then it is canceled.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן quotes a case to show that words alone can cancel an earlier statement. This attacks ריש לקיש's position.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sending the שליח was done with words, and the cancellation is also just words. Yet the cancellation works. That fits רבי יוחנן's view that speech can cancel speech, against ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: Agent, someone sent to act for another person

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan raised an objection to Reish Lakish:
One who sends a get to his wife,
and he caught up with the agent,
or he sent another agent after him,
and said to him:
"The get that I gave you is canceled" —
it is canceled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side discussion about thought in טומאה, רבי יוחנן goes on the attack against ריש לקיש.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that speech cannot cancel earlier speech
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Appointing a שליח is done with words, and canceling it is also words. Since the cancellation works, speech does cancel speech.

steps.title: ריש לקיש is disproven
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא declares that ריש לקיש's view has been refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The refutation of ריש לקיש is a real refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that רבי יוחנן's challenge works and ריש לקיש has no answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No answer is given for ריש לקיש, so his position falls. The idea that speech can cancel speech now stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation, a challenge with no answer that knocks down a view

phrases.english: The refutation of Reish Lakish is a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge from step 14.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ריש לקיש is refuted. Speech can cancel earlier speech.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יוחנן, even in the first case
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה is like רבי יוחנן, even in the case of a woman who accepted money for קידושין and then changed her mind.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה follows רבי יוחנן, even in the first case. One could argue that handing money to a woman is different, because it is like an action. Even so, speech comes and cancels speech.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final הלכה like רבי יוחנן. It stresses that this holds even in the harder first case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, a woman took money for קידושין and then changed her mind. You might think receiving money is like an action, and words cannot undo an action. The גמרא rules that her later words still cancel her earlier agreement.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical הלכה, the final ruling
The first one, here meaning the first version of the argument

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה is like רבי יוחנן: a spoken statement can cancel an earlier spoken statement, even after a woman received money for קידושין.

phrases.english: And the halacha follows Rabbi Yochanan,
even in the first case.
phrases.notes: He means the first version of their argument, about the woman who changes her mind after taking the money.

phrases.english: And even though one could say:
giving money into a woman's hand is different,
since it counts like an action,
even so,
speech comes and cancels speech.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After ריש לקיש is refuted, the גמרא states the practical ruling.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the practical rule: a woman who changes her mind before her קידושין take effect can undo them by speaking.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה is like רבי יוחנן in both versions: speech cancels speech, even where money was given.

steps.title: This seems to clash with רב נחמן's ruling about reusing a canceled גט
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how ruling like רבי יוחנן fits with ruling like רב נחמן, who says a husband may later divorce with a גט he canceled.
steps.simpleTranslation: One הלכה contradicts another. You said the הלכה is like רבי יוחנן. But we hold the הלכה is like רב נחמן. They asked: can the husband later divorce with that same גט? רב נחמן says he can. רב ששת says he cannot. And we hold like רב נחמן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a clash between two rulings that are both accepted as הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If speech cancels speech, then when the husband said 'the גט is canceled,' the גט should be dead. Yet רב נחמן, whom we follow, says the husband can still use that same גט later. That seems to show the גט was never truly canceled.

keyTerms.meaning: We hold, it is our accepted rule
They asked, a question raised in the בית מדרש
He can go back and divorce with it

phrases.english: One halacha contradicts another halacha.
You said: the halacha follows Rabbi Yochanan,
but we hold the halacha follows Rav Nachman,
for they asked:
May he go back and divorce with it?
phrases.notes: "It" is the same גט the husband just canceled through his שליח.

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: חוֹזֵר וּמְגָרֵשׁ בּוֹ,
phrases.english: Rav Nachman says: he may go back and divorce with it;

phrases.aramaic: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר: אֵינוֹ חוֹזֵר וּמְגָרֵשׁ בּוֹ.
phrases.english: Rav Sheshet says: he may not go back and divorce with it.

phrases.aramaic: וְקַיְימָא לַן הִילְכְתָא כְּוָתֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן!
phrases.english: And we hold the halacha follows Rav Nachman!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the new ruling from step 16 against another accepted ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the הלכה follows רבי יוחנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If speech fully cancels the גט, it should be useless afterward. רב נחמן, whom we follow, lets the husband reuse it, so the cancellation seems not to work.

steps.title: He canceled the שליח, not the גט
steps.stepSummary: The husband's words cancel the שליח's mission, but the גט itself stays a valid document.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is true that he canceled the שליח as a שליח. But he did not cancel the גט as a גט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the clash by separating the שליח from the גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the husband speaks, he ends the שליח's job, just as רבי יוחנן says speech can do. The paper itself stays a kosher גט, so the husband can use it again, as רב נחמן says. Both rulings stand.

keyTerms.meaning: In the role of, as far as its status as

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the husband's words destroyed the גט. They only ended the שליח's job. The document itself is still a valid גט.
steps.whatToRemember: Speech cancels the שליח's appointment, but the גט itself stays valid and can be used again.

phrases.english: Granted that he canceled him from being an agent,
he did not cancel it from being a get.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: the agency is canceled, but the document stays valid
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Saying 'the גט is canceled' kills the גט itself, so it can never be used again.
steps.terutzMaskana: The words only end the שליח's mission. The גט stays valid, so רבי יוחנן and רב נחמן do not clash.

steps.title: רב and שמואל argue about the second man's קידושין
steps.stepSummary: On the משנה's ruling 'she is betrothed to the second,' רב says this lasts forever. שמואל says it lasts only until the thirty days end, and then the first man's קידושין take over.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: she is betrothed to the second man. רב says: she is betrothed to the second man forever. שמואל says: she is betrothed to the second man only until thirty days pass. After thirty days, the second man's קידושין fall away and the first man's קידושין become complete.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה and brings an argument between רב and שמואל about how long the second man's קידושין last.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה's case, the first man said 'be betrothed to me after thirty days,' and a second man betrothed her before then. רב says the second man's קידושין are fully valid for good. שמואל says the first man's קידושין can still take effect at day thirty and push the second man out.

keyTerms.meaning: She is betrothed to the second man
They become complete, they take full effect

phrases.english: She is betrothed to the second man.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה: the first man said 'after thirty days,' and a second man betrothed her before the thirty days ended.

phrases.english: Rav says: She is betrothed to the second forever.

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אֲמַר: מְקוּדֶּשֶׁת לַשֵּׁנִי עַד שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם,
phrases.english: And Shmuel says: She is betrothed to the second until thirty days pass.

phrases.aramaic: לְאַחַר שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם פָּקְעִי קִידּוּשֵׁי שֵׁנִי
phrases.english: After thirty days, the second man's betrothal lapses,
and the first man's betrothal becomes complete.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: מְקוּדֶּשֶׁת לַשֵּׁנִי לְעוֹלָם, וּשְׁמוּאֵל אֲמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic on a new line of the משנה. It does not continue the discussion about the שליח and the גט.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: the second man's קידושין are permanent. שמואל: they last only until day thirty, and then the first man's קידושין take effect.

steps.title: How can the second man's קידושין just fall away?
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא is puzzled by שמואל's view. By what means could the second man's קידושין lapse?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא sat and found it difficult: By what means do the second man's קידושין fall away?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא challenges שמואל's opinion and asks how valid קידושין could simply end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the second man betrothed her, the first man's קידושין had not started yet, so she was free. The second man's קידושין were therefore fully valid. Nothing seems able to cancel them later, so the first man's קידושין should never be able to take effect.

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַב חִסְדָּא וְקָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Chisda sat and found it difficult:
By what means does the second man's betrothal lapse?

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב רַב חִסְדָּא וְקָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks שמואל's opinion from step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's claim that the second man's קידושין lapse after thirty days
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The second man's קידושין took hold while she was free, so nothing should be able to undo them later.

steps.title: The argument was taught on a different case
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that רב חסדא learned the argument on the first case of the משנה. רב יהודה learned it on the later case, where there is no difficulty.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said to him: You, Master, teach this argument on the first case, and so it is difficult for you. רב יהודה teaches it on the later case, and so it is not difficult for him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers רב חסדא by saying he attached the argument to the wrong case in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question only works if the first man said simply 'after thirty days.' רב יהודה taught the argument on the case of 'from now and after thirty days.' In that case the first man's קידושין may have started right away, so the second man's קידושין can lapse. The גמרא now sets up רב יהודה's version.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause of the משנה
The later clause of the משנה
Master, a respectful way of saying 'you'

steps.confusionAlert: רב יוסף is not saying שמואל is wrong. He is saying the argument between רב and שמואל was really about a different case in the משנה.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said to him:

phrases.aramaic: מָר אַרֵישָׁא מַתְנֵי לַהּ וְקַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: The Master teaches it on the first clause, and so he finds it difficult;

phrases.aramaic: רַב יְהוּדָה אַסֵּיפָא מַתְנֵי לַהּ וְלָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda teaches it on the later clause, and so he does not find it difficult.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר אַרֵישָׁא מַתְנֵי לַהּ וְקַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב חסדא's question from step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moving the argument onto a different clause of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The argument is about 'after thirty days,' so the second man's קידושין cannot lapse.
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument is about 'from now and after thirty days,' where the second man's קידושין can lapse.

steps.title: רב יהודה's version: the 'from now and after thirty days' case
steps.stepSummary: On 'from now and after thirty days,' רב says the doubt about whether she is betrothed lasts forever. שמואל says it lasts only until day thirty, and then the first man's קידושין take over.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'From now and after thirty days,' and so on. רב says: it is uncertain whether she is betrothed or not, forever. שמואל says: it is uncertain whether she is betrothed or not only until thirty days. After thirty days, the second man's קידושין fall away and the first man's קידושין become complete.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רב יהודה's version of the argument, now placed on the case of 'from now and after thirty days.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the first man's words are unclear. They might mean his קידושין already started 'from now.' So each man's hold on her is in doubt. רב says that doubt never goes away. שמואל says it ends at day thirty, and then she belongs to the first man.

keyTerms.meaning: From now and after thirty days
She is betrothed and not betrothed, meaning it is a doubt
And so on (the rest of the quote)

phrases.english: "From now and after thirty days," and so on.
phrases.notes: This is the later case in the משנה. There, if another man betroths her in the meantime, it is a doubt whether she is betrothed.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב: מְקוּדֶּשֶׁת וְאֵינָהּ מְקוּדֶּשֶׁת לְעוֹלָם.
phrases.english: Rav says: She is betrothed and not betrothed, forever.
And Shmuel says: She is betrothed and not betrothed
only until thirty days;
after thirty days, the second man's betrothal lapses
and the first man's betrothal becomes complete.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the version of the argument that רב יוסף mentioned in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: the doubt lasts forever. שמואל: the doubt lasts until day thirty, and then the first man's קידושין win.

steps.title: The root of the argument: condition or change of mind?
steps.stepSummary: רב is unsure whether 'from now and after thirty days' was a condition or a change of mind. שמואל is sure it was a condition.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב is unsure whether it was a condition or a change of mind. שמואל is sure that it was a condition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind רב's and שמואל's opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If it was a condition, it means 'from now, as long as I don't change my mind within thirty days.' Then at day thirty his קידושין count from the start and push out the second man. If it was a change of mind, he took back 'from now,' and his קידושין only start after thirty days. רב cannot decide between these, so the doubt never ends. שמואל is sure it was a condition, so the doubt ends at day thirty.

keyTerms.meaning: Taking back one's words, a change of mind

steps.whatToRemember: In 'from now and after thirty days,' רב keeps the doubt forever because he is unsure whether it was a condition or a change of mind. שמואל treats it as a condition, so once thirty days pass, the first man's קידושין count from the beginning and the second man's fall away.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answers רב חסדא's question. If it was a condition, the first man's קידושין can reach back to the start, and that is how the second man's קידושין fall away.

phrases.english: Rav is unsure

phrases.aramaic: אִי תְּנָאָה הֲוַאי, אִי חֲזָרָה הֲוַאי.
phrases.english: whether it was a condition or a change of mind.
phrases.notes: A 'condition' means: from now, unless I change my mind in thirty days. A 'change of mind' means: he took back 'from now.'

phrases.english: Shmuel is certain that it was a condition.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְרַב מְסַפְּקָא לֵיהּ אִי תְּנָאָה הֲוַאי, אִי חֲזָרָה הֲוַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the two opinions in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: unsure whether it was a condition or a change of mind. שמואל: certain it was a condition.

steps.title: רב and שמואל match an older argument about a גט
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רב and שמואל's argument matches the argument of the חכמים and רבי about a גט given 'from today and after death.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב and שמואל argue in the same way as these תנאים. A ברייתא teaches: if a man gives a גט 'from today and after death,' the חכמים say it is a גט and not a גט, meaning it is a doubt. רבי says: a גט like this is a valid גט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא connects the רב–שמואל argument to an older argument from a ברייתא. The case there is a man who gives his wife a גט that should work 'from today and after my death.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים are unsure. Maybe he meant 'from today,' so the גט works. Or maybe he changed his mind to 'after death,' and a גט cannot work after death. רבי is sure it was a condition, so the גט is valid. This lines up with רב, who has a doubt, and שמואל, who says it was a condition.

keyTerms.meaning: The sages of the משנה period
It is a גט and it is not a גט: a case of doubt

phrases.english: And in the dispute of these tanna'im
phrases.notes: The גמרא leaves out who is arguing here: it means רב and שמואל argue just like these older sages.

phrases.english: As it is taught:
"From today and after death"
It is a get and it is not a get
These are the words of the Sages.
Rabbi says: a get like this is a valid get.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Places the רב–שמואל argument from step 23 inside an earlier תנאים argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב matches the חכמים, who have a doubt. שמואל matches רבי, who treats the words as a condition.

steps.title: Why not just say whose view is the הלכה?
steps.stepSummary: If the argument already exists among the תנאים, רב could just say 'the הלכה follows the חכמים,' and שמואל could say 'the הלכה follows רבי.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let רב say: the הלכה follows the רבנן. And let שמואל say: the הלכה follows רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב and שמואל spelled out their own opinions. They could have simply sided with one of the תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If their argument is exactly the same as the old one, saying it again seems unnecessary. A short line about which view is the הלכה would have been enough.

phrases.english: Then let Rav say: the halacha follows the Rabbis
And let Shmuel say: the halacha follows Rabbi!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges why the argument needed to be stated again, given the match shown in step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for רב and שמואל to state their own argument
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the argument is identical to the תנאים argument, simply ruling like one side would have been enough.

steps.title: רב's view had to be said directly
steps.stepSummary: Had רב only said 'the הלכה follows the חכמים,' we might think he agrees with שמואל about קידושין, because a man who betroths wants to bring her close.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is necessary. If רב had said 'the הלכה follows the רבנן,' I would have thought: there, with a גט, he is trying to push her away. But here, with קידושין, he is trying to bring her close, so רב would agree with שמואל that it was a condition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that each statement was needed. This step explains why רב had to state his view directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a גט, a man may be unsure and pull back, so a doubt makes sense. With קידושין, he wants her as soon as possible, so we might think even רב sees 'from now' as a firm condition. רב's own words teach that he has a doubt even in קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary to say both

phrases.english: It is necessary.
For if Rav had said:
The halacha follows the Rabbis
I would have said:
There, he comes to distance her
phrases.notes: 'There' means the גט case, where he is sending her away.

phrases.english: But here, where he comes to draw her near
I might say he agrees with Shmuel
That it was a condition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 25 for רב's side.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: showing each statement teaches something new
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב would agree with שמואל in קידושין, since the man wants to bring her close.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב has a doubt even in קידושין, so he had to say so directly.

steps.title: שמואל's view had to be said directly too
steps.stepSummary: Had שמואל only said 'the הלכה follows רבי,' we might think he agrees with רב about קידושין, because קידושין can really take effect after thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if שמואל had said 'the הלכה follows רבי,' I would have thought: that is only there, because a גט cannot work after death. But here, where קידושין can work after thirty days, he would agree with רב. So it is necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes the answer by explaining why שמואל also had to state his view directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a גט, 'after death' makes no sense because a גט cannot work then, so he must have meant a condition. With קידושין, 'after thirty days' is a real option, so maybe he truly changed his mind. שמואל's own words teach that even here it is a condition.

keyTerms.meaning: A גט cannot take effect after death

steps.whatToRemember: Both רב and שמואל had to speak directly. גט and קידושין each have a reason that could have flipped the other side, so a plain 'the הלכה follows so-and-so' would not have been enough.

phrases.english: And if Shmuel had said:
The halacha follows Rabbi
I would have said:

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם הוּא דְּאֵין גֵּט לְאַחַר מִיתָה.
phrases.english: It is there, because there is no get after death.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא דְּיֵשׁ קִידּוּשִׁין לְאַחַר שְׁלֹשִׁים,
phrases.english: But here, where there is kiddushin after thirty days
I might say he agrees with Rav
So it is necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of the צריכותא, covering שמואל's side.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: showing each statement teaches something new
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל would agree with רב in קידושין, since קידושין after thirty days is a real possibility.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל holds it is a condition even in קידושין, so he had to say so directly.

steps.title: אביי sets up a case with two men, following רב's view
steps.stepSummary: אביי begins a case based on רב's view. One man says 'from now and after thirty days,' then another says 'from now and after twenty days.'
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: According to רב's reasoning, suppose one man came and said to her, 'You are betrothed to me from now and after thirty days.' Then another man came and said to her, 'You are betrothed to me from now and after twenty days.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי is setting up a new case to show what happens under רב's view. The ruling comes in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רב, each man's words are in doubt: did he mean 'from now' or 'after the time period'? With two men and two different time periods, the doubts overlap. אביי will work out who she is betrothed to.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
And according to Rav's reasoning
One man came and said to her:
"You are hereby betrothed to me
From now and after thirty days"
And another man came and said to her:
"You are hereby betrothed to me
From now and after twenty days"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the צריכותא, opens a new case that applies רב's view of doubt.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case of two men with overlapping time periods. The ruling follows in the next part.
